text: Then all the commanders of the forces came forward—Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest—

versions.text: Then all the commanders of the forces, along with Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest, came forward
versions.explanation: The long list of subjects delays the verb to the very end, which is hard to follow when read aloud. Placing the verb early and setting the list off keeps the Hebrew content while improving oral flow.

text: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Let our plea come before you: pray for us to the LORD your God, for all this remnant. For we are left few out of many, as your own eyes can see.
Let the LORD your God tell us the way we should go and what we should do."

Jeremiah the prophet answered them, "I have heard you. I will indeed pray to the LORD your God as you have asked, and whatever the LORD answers you, I will tell you; I will keep nothing back from you."
Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act on everything the LORD your God sends you to tell us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God."
Ten days later the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
So he called for Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, and for all the people from the least to the greatest,
and said to them: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says, the one to whom you sent me to lay your plea before him:

versions.text: and said to them: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says—the one to whom you sent me to present your plea before him:
versions.explanation: "to present your plea before him" duplicates the relative pronoun with a resumptive "him," making the clause clumsy in English; "lay your plea before him" also better reflects the Hebrew idiom hippil techinnah (to let a supplication fall before someone).

text: If you will indeed remain in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I relent of the disaster I have brought upon you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear. Do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
I will grant you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and restore you to your own land.

versions.text: I will show you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and let you return to your own soil.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has God "giving" compassion (through the king of Babylon), and heshiv means "restore/bring back," which is stronger than "let you return." "Your own soil" is an unnatural phrase for oral reading; "your own land" is the normal English rendering of admah here.

text: But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the voice of the LORD your God,
saying, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no sound of the trumpet, and never go hungry for bread—there we will settle,'

versions.text: saying, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no sound of the trumpet, and hunger for no bread—there we will settle,'
versions.explanation: "Hunger for no bread" reads as a lack of desire for bread rather than a lack of famine. "Never go hungry for bread" conveys the Hebrew sense of not starving and reads more naturally aloud.

text: then hear the word of the LORD, you remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you are determined to go to Egypt and settle there,
then the sword you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow close behind you into Egypt, and there you will die.
All the men who are determined to go to Egypt and settle there will die by the sword, by famine, and by plague. Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I am bringing upon them.

For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: As my anger and wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become an object of cursing and horror, of condemnation and reproach, and you will never see this place again.
The LORD has spoken to you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Be certain of this: I have warned you today
that you went astray at the cost of your own lives. For you sent me to the LORD your God, saying, 'Pray for us to the LORD our God; tell us everything the LORD our God says, and we will do it.'
I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God in anything he sent me to tell you.
So now be certain of this: you will die by the sword, by famine, and by plague in the place where you want to go and settle."
